description: Explicit snapshot of four public companion studies; not a live index.

documents.title: Quantum Risk Observatory / Base market
documents.text:
Four correlated option positions. Revalue the full book at a 21-day horizon and compare three simulation designs at matched path budgets.
99% value at risk: 683.8816824040545 USD
99% expected shortfall: 764.1748139172402 USD
99% potential exposure: 1541.6003364587596 USD
Scenarios: 32768.0 paths
Correlated GBM terminal simulation; Black–Scholes revaluation of remaining six-month option maturities. Positions and currency scale are explicit.
Randomized Sobol and antithetic designs are compared with independent Monte Carlo using 12 separate seeds at four budgets. The high-budget independent reference is itself a simulation estimate.
VaR is an empirical loss quantile; expected shortfall averages observations in the empirical tail. PFE uses positive future book value, not losses.
Limitations:
Illustrative synthetic asset parameters, not calibrated market data or an investment recommendation.
Lognormal dynamics omit stochastic volatility, defaults, liquidity and funding; tail estimates remain model dependent.
The chart compares mean-loss error. It does not establish quantum advantage or tail-quantile confidence intervals.

documents.title: Quantum Risk Observatory / Quantum oracle
documents.text:
An eight-scenario register and a payoff ancilla, explicit unitary preparation, amplitude amplification and maximum-likelihood estimation.
Exact encoded expectation: 0.2495 
Estimated expectation: 0.25018020656764217 
Oracle preparation calls: 8960.0 
Logical qubits: 4.0 
Prepare amplitudes sqrt(p_j(1-f_j)) and sqrt(p_j f_j) on the scenario/ancilla basis. Householder state preparation is unitary and explicitly inverted inside the Grover operator.
A Bernoulli likelihood over Grover powers estimates the bounded expectation. The profile-likelihood bounding interval is 0.24740 to 0.25293; it is an asymptotic, potentially disconnected likelihood set.
At the same 8960 preparation-query budget a recorded direct Bernoulli estimate is 0.24967. One random trial is not a comparative performance study.
Limitations:
Dense unitary simulation is exponential and is not a compiled fault-tolerant implementation.
This bounded discrete payoff is separate from the portfolio's unbounded continuous loss; no claim that the oracle directly estimates its VaR is made.
State preparation, inverse preparation and Grover queries are counted. Device gates, errors, compilation and classical inference costs are not hidden in a speedup claim.

documents.title: Quantum Decision Studio / Constrained allocation
documents.text:
Eight synthetic assets, exactly three holdings, turnover costs and correlated risk. Compare a number-preserving quantum ansatz with exhaustive enumeration and classical local search.
Exact minimum cost: -0.03829410872888889 
QAOA expected cost: -0.03078526296591523 
Optimal-sample probability: 10.528668658051656 %
Feasible configurations: 56.0 
Objective = 4 wᵀΣw − μᵀw + 0.003‖w−w_previous‖₁; equal weights on exactly three of eight assets. Covariance is positive definite by construction.
Depth-2 cost phases alternate with an exact ring-XY mixer in the 56-state feasible sector. Six seeded Nelder–Mead restarts each have a 350-iteration cap. Uniform feasible-state preparation is assumed, not compiled.
Exact enumeration gives A, D, H. Swap local search gives A, D, H, cost -0.038294, after 30 neighbour evaluations. The ansatz is not claimed to outperform either baseline.
Limitations:
Synthetic forward-looking means/covariance: no historical backtest or investment claim. Small exact simulation is the reference, not evidence of scalability.
Mixer construction and dense exponentiation operate in a constrained subspace; physical preparation, compiled gates and measurement overhead are not benchmarked.
Uniform probability mixing is a sensitivity model, not calibrated gate noise. Both expected objective and success probability must be inspected.

documents.title: Quantum Decision Studio / Correlated electrons
documents.text:
A spinful two-site Hubbard dimer isolates the competition between electron hopping and on-site repulsion. A symmetry-preserving variational state is checked against exact and analytic ground-state energies.
Maximum energy error: 5.551115123125783e-16 t
Spin orbitals: 4.0 
Sector dimension: 4.0 
Double occupancy at U/t=8: 0.05278640618919383 
Construct −t Σσ(c†₀σc₁σ+h.c.) + UΣᵢnᵢ↑nᵢ↓ using fermionic parity signs; restrict to one spin-up and one spin-down electron.
Three real two-level Givens rotations span the four-state real sector. Three seeded BFGS starts minimize the statevector energy for each interaction.
Each result obeys the variational bound and agrees with E₀=(U−√(U²+16t²))/2 within 10⁻⁶ t. Double occupancy is a separate observable, not inferred from a fitted curve.
Limitations:
This is an effective correlated-electron benchmark, not an ab initio molecule or a battery-material prediction. It is a foundation for extending the battery-design theme.
The ansatz can span this tiny real sector; success does not demonstrate a scalable chemistry algorithm.
No finite-shot Pauli measurement, molecular geometry, basis-set error, device noise or battery voltage is represented.

documents.title: Market Replay Studio / Balanced flow
documents.text:
Balanced flow: a price/time-priority book, cancellable orders, inventory-constrained quoting and stale quotes. Replay the managed policy, then compare net results across sixteen paired seeds.
Managed net after liquidation: 607.9 ticks
Paired improvement vs symmetric: -497.64374999999995 ticks
Paired difference standard error: 42.4131504456951 ticks
Cash / inventory violations: 0.0 
Orders match at the resting price, best price then FIFO. Partial fills and owner-checked cancellations use the same book as the replay, with integer price/quantity accounting.
All trader accounts conserve aggregate cash and inventory after every batch. Agent fees are a separate external charge of 0.05 tick/unit; the net ledger includes that fee sink. Final liquidation executes through five refreshed LP levels, ten units each, starting at mid ±3 ticks. Price slippage and fees are included.
Inventory is bounded at ±20 units through quote sizing. Latency means quotes refresh every five batches; background liquidity and marketable external orders continue each batch.
Sixteen independent seeds compare policies with identical pre-generated price, order-size and flow draws. In the adverse regime, 70% of eligible flow is informed by the next reference move; this privileged signal is unavailable to the agent.
Limitations:
Synthetic event flow and exogenous reference prices are not calibrated exchange data. No claim of profitable live trading is made.
Background refreshes may trade against stale agent quotes; losses from those crossings are included. The agent does not control market impact or reference prices.
Latency is measured in event batches, not network nanoseconds. Hidden liquidity, auctions, credit limits and exchange-specific order types are omitted.
Recorded replay uses seed 1729; summary uncertainty uses separate paired seeds 100–115. Mark-to-mid equity differs from final liquidated net.

documents.title: RegimeLab / Stable regime
documents.text:
Predict next-day realized variance from six causal return features. Compare a small neural network, regularized regression, persistence and an expanding-window adaptation under a controlled volatility shock.
Frozen ridge MAE: 0.4030305544093381 
Expanding ridge MAE: 0.40378462688112504 
Nominal interval coverage: 90.0 %
Observed test coverage: 91.07468123861567 %
Seed 73: Gaussian innovations with v[t]=ω+α r[t−1]²+β v[t−1]. Baseline (ω,α,β)=(0.025,0.10,0.84); from day 1450 the stress case uses (0.12,0.16,0.84), deliberately α+β=1. Features at close t: squared return, 5/20-day variance, return, 20-day mean absolute return and 5-day mean return. Label: r² at t+1.
Training targets <1000; validation 1001–1199 chooses ridge penalty 0.01; calibration 1201–1449 sets a finite-sample absolute-residual quantile; test starts 1451. Scaling is fitted on training only. Embargoed boundaries prevent target overlap.
A 6→12→1 tanh MLP trains for 350 full-batch epochs on log1p variance, with fixed settings and training-only normalization. No claim that this architecture is optimal is made.
Frozen ridge interval radius = 0.860936; lower endpoint clipped at zero. Expanding ridge refits every 60 targets, uses only earlier observed labels and keeps the previously selected penalty. It does not reuse the frozen interval as an adaptive guarantee.
Limitations:
Synthetic heteroscedastic data tests a known mechanism; it is not a historical market backtest or evidence of alpha. Squared returns are noisy variance proxies.
The post-break stress has unit variance persistence and no finite stationary unconditional variance. It is a deliberately nonstationary stress, not a stable high-volatility regime.
Serial dependence and deliberate distribution shift violate exchangeability. Split-conformal intervals here are diagnostics; 90% empirical coverage is not guaranteed under these conditions.
Mean absolute error, RMSE and QLIKE can rank models differently. QLIKE uses a 10⁻⁵ positivity floor, disclosed because near-zero forecasts can dominate it.
Only one process seed is shown. Hyperparameters are selected without test data, but broad model selection uncertainty and transaction costs are not quantified.
